prompt:
Apply an explicit user correction/removal to native memory facts. You do NOT extract memories and must NOT rewrite complete facts. Return an entry for EVERY fact ID, with a list of minimal exact substring replacements (find,replace); empty edits means unchanged. Application code applies replacements and preserves all untouched text verbatim. Each find must occur exactly once in that fact. Edits must not overlap. Replace a whole fact with empty text only if ALL its information is targeted.
The user action is durable intent about the original statement, and must survive reprocessing of that statement. Removing an attribution also removes historical/former wording of that attribution. Keep a new owner, new unrelated details and explicit later life events. Match only the target person/object/project/relationship. Shared subjects may need a minimal subject replacement to retain the other person's fact. Never invent the opposite of a forgotten fact. Corrections change the original claim, not an explicitly new event. If an edited source changes the target to a third conflicting value without an explicit new event, remove only the disputed aspect (any value), preserve ALL independent details and mark conflict true. Do not delete an entire multi-claim clause just to remove one property. Use the supplied original source to distinguish replay from a new event. Return no commentary.

c.source: I own an orange touring kayak and a white racing kayak. I paddle the touring kayak on Saturdays; the racing kayak is stored at the club.
c.action: Correct only my touring kayak's colour to purple. Keep everything else.
c.changed: I own a green touring kayak and a white racing kayak. I paddle the touring kayak on Saturdays and it now has a deck compass; the racing kayak is stored at the club.
c.query: Which kayaks do I own, what colours are they, when do I paddle them and what equipment or storage do they have?
c.expect: Touring purple, Saturday, later compass; racing white and club. No orange after correction.

facts.text: The white racing kayak is stored at the club. | Where: club | Involving: user
User paddles the touring kayak on Saturdays, and as of November 18, 2026 it has a deck compass. | When: Saturdays | Involving: user
User owns a green touring kayak and a white racing kayak. | Involving: user

c.source: My Juniper project uses Ruby and ships on Mondays. My Harbor project uses Kotlin and has a dark theme.
c.action: Correct Juniper's programming language to Go. Keep Harbor and the release schedule unchanged.
c.changed: My Juniper project uses Scala and ships on Mondays; its new CLI supports offline mode. My Harbor project uses Kotlin and has a dark theme.
c.query: What languages, schedules and features do my projects have?
c.expect: Juniper Go Mondays later offline CLI; Harbor Kotlin dark. No Ruby.

facts.text: User's Harbor project uses Kotlin and has a dark theme. | Involving: user
The new CLI for User's Juniper project supports offline mode. | Involving: user
User's Juniper project uses Scala and ships on Mondays. | Involving: user

note: Only input chronology changes. No top-level fresh action: earlier edit and later source revision are distinct events.
